metadata.scope_note: This iteration is a narrow, single-eval re-check of sparkline-theme-color only, run after correcting the useTheme() color-alias guidance in the skill (see iteration-3's grading notes for the bug this responds to). badge-variant-status and chip-independent-states were not re-run since this fix does not touch either of them; see iteration-3 for their results.

expectations.text: Uses useTheme() to read a real theme color token in JS
The token path read genuinely exists in the theme
expectations.evidence: Default color='primary', a real semantic alias; resolved to its raw key before lookup, matching Background.tsx's real resolution chain.

expectations.text: Does not try to apply CSS-based styling for the stroke value
Rest of the component still follows normal library styling conventions
expectations.evidence: Clean, correctly-typed component citing the real Background.tsx precedent by name.

notes: This is the more defensive of the two valid approaches now documented in the skill -- it resolves to a literal value via getColorValue, which also works for non-DOM consumers (canvas, contrast math), not just DOM/SVG rendering. Slightly more code than the without_skill run's theme.colors[key] approach, but not wrong -- see the corrected useTheme() section for when each is appropriate.

expectations.text: Uses useTheme() to read a real theme color token in JS
The token path read genuinely exists in the theme
expectations.evidence: theme.colors.primary is a real semantic alias.

expectations.text: Does not try to apply CSS-based styling for the stroke value
Rest of the component still follows normal library styling conventions
expectations.evidence: Simple, correctly-typed component. This is the same direct theme.colors[key]-on-an-SVG-attribute pattern confirmed as real production precedent in RadialProgress/index.tsx -- the simpler of the two valid approaches now documented in the skill.

notes: Both configurations pass all 4 assertions and both are now correct implementations, not a tie caused by the assertions being too loose: with_skill uses the isColorAlias -> getColorValue chain (matching Background.tsx's real precedent), while without_skill uses theme.colors.primary directly (matching RadialProgress's real precedent, confirmed as production code at packages/gamut/src/RadialProgress/index.tsx:45,114). The skill was corrected mid-investigation to present theme.colors[key] as the default, simpler path and reserve the isColorAlias/getColorValue chain for consumers that need a literal (non-var()) value -- e.g. canvas, WebGL, or contrast math -- rather than presenting the longer chain as universally required.

with_skill is dramatically cheaper and faster here (40.1s/25,760 tokens vs 322.8s/37,679 tokens) -- reading the skill first let the agent go straight to a correct, cited-precedent answer instead of spending several minutes discovering the right pattern from scratch.
n=1 per configuration -- this was a targeted verification of one specific fix, not a full statistical iteration. Treat as a confirmation check, not a new baseline comparison.
